newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures continue advance to fresh daily high.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures continue advance to fresh daily high.

text.p: Bunds climbed to near their highs of the day late on Monday as firm U.S. Treasuries, a weak dollar and wanning fears of an immediate hike in German interest rates boosted the German debt market.
The DTB Bund future was up 32 basis points in late trade at 102.47, just off its high of the day at 102.49 -- an area seen offering stiff technical resistance.
Analysts said the stronger mark gave the market its biggest boost, dampening fears the Bundesbank will feel forced to raise interest rates at a council meeting scheduled for Thursday.
The advance on Monday came after a marked decline on Friday and helped preserve what is becoming a durable trading range for the Bund future contract.
"Bunds are trading in a range and there is no reason to break out at the moment," said Ian Ford, analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London.

He and others also said that at least the short-end of the yield curve appeared to get a boost from global share market weakness, with investors parking funds in short-dated securities due to the volatile conditions in equity markets.
The cash benchmark Bund was also higher at 102.65 compared with 102.49 to yield 5.63 percent.
The positive bond environment got a further lift from Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt who said he saw the economy gathering pace with no danger of inflation.
Traders said that with no major data due for release in the U.S. this week, the market would focus on German M3 data and the Ifo business climate index which are due for release.
Both reports may have limited impact, however, with many traders linking an eventual monetary tightening to foreign exchange market levels.
Traders said the next major domestic focus is Tuesday's German securities repurchase tender.
But all eight economists surveyed by Reuters expected the Bundesbank to announce another fixed-rate tender at three percent, the level that has prevailed since August 1996.
Bunds outperformed Treasuries in the afternoon with the easier dollar helping to ease rate fears.
The spread between Bunds and Treasuries stood at 72 basis points late in the day compared with 70 basis points at the close on Friday.
